nodes.label: Avoid Premature Abstraction
nodes.rationale: The architecture exists to protect business logic, not to maximize the number of interfaces or classes: prefer Simple + Testable + Decoupled over Complex + Over-engineered.

nodes.label: Aggregate Owns DailyActivities Indexed by Day
nodes.community_name: Mutation Use Cases (Create/Complete/Update DailyActivity, Create ScopeMonitoring)
nodes.norm_label: aggregate owns dailyactivities indexed by day
nodes.rationale: Uniqueness of one activity per scope per day is guaranteed by the aggregate via dict[date, DailyActivity]; the relationship is unidirectional so a DailyActivity never references its ScopeMonitoring.

nodes.label: Atomic ScopeMonitoring Creation
nodes.community_name: Mutation Use Cases (Create/Complete/Update DailyActivity, Create ScopeMonitoring)
nodes.rationale: CreateScopeMonitoringUseCase creates several scopes (uuid4 ids) atomically: a duplicate name or any invalid line means nothing is persisted.

nodes.label: Day Is Not a Class (datetime.date as value object)
nodes.community_name: Mutation Use Cases (Create/Complete/Update DailyActivity, Create ScopeMonitoring)
nodes.norm_label: day is not a class (datetime.date as value object)
nodes.rationale: A day has no identity or business behavior beyond its value, and datetime.date is already an immutable value object. 'All activities of a day' is an outbound-port query, not a domain structure.

nodes.label: Dependency Injection and Composition Root
nodes.rationale: Dependencies must be injected rather than instantiated inside business logic, and concrete wiring happens only in a Composition Root at the outermost layer.

nodes.label: Dependency Rule (Adapters → Ports → Application → Domain)
nodes.rationale: Dependencies must always point toward the application core so the domain stays independent of infrastructure; imports of flask/sqlalchemy/requests in domain code are explicitly forbidden.

nodes.label: Domain Error Handling and Adapter Translation
nodes.norm_label: domain error handling and adapter translation
nodes.rationale: Business errors are expressed as domain exceptions; infrastructure exceptions must not leak into the domain and are translated at the adapter boundary.

nodes.label: Framework Isolation
nodes.rationale: Frameworks and infrastructure libraries are implementation details kept at the outer layers so a framework can be replaced without rewriting the domain.

nodes.label: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters)
nodes.rationale: The architecture exists to protect the application core from external technical concerns; code quality and architectural integrity take priority over implementation speed.

nodes.label: Audit Trail (best-effort mutation journal)
nodes.rationale: Every mutation is traced with actor, action, scope, day and a field-by-field before/after diff, but writes are best-effort: an audit failure must not fail the business request, and no-op changes are not logged.

nodes.label: Quadrigramme Bootstrap Exemption
nodes.rationale: Once a project owns at least one scope the login quadrigramme must match an official_main or official_backup, but while a project has no scope any quadrigramme is accepted so the very first scope can still be created.

nodes.label: Same-Origin nginx Reverse Proxy (no CORS)
nodes.rationale: nginx serves the React SPA and proxies /scope-monitorings to the api, keeping everything same-origin so no CORS configuration is required.

nodes.label: Documentation Synchronization Requirement
nodes.rationale: AGENT.md is a living document and source of truth; a feature is not complete until all affected documentation has been updated in the same change.

nodes.label: Test-Driven Development (RED/GREEN/REFACTOR)
nodes.rationale: TDD is mandatory for new behavior: write a failing test first, implement the minimum to pass without speculative functionality, then refactor while keeping tests green.
